prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form, which made possible incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep B024 as a single prize part with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. Because all six of us arrived at the same configuration, I tested it against the strongest alternatives, as Sandberg asked. B011 has a complete chain from engineered receptor design to clinical remission, but its credit gap (Eshhar and the early chimeric receptor work) is structural and is made more visible by a two-name prize. B020 is a clean, mature discovery of a basic cellular signalling pathway, but its link to disease treatment is still thin. B045 is a tool prize with six claimants for three places, and B034 and B047 have larger credit gaps or a weaker conceptual step. Only B024 combines a physiological discovery of this kind with independent, replicated evidence through to large randomized outcome trials in diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal endpoints. The three credited names each cover a distinct step: native GLP-1 physiology and secretion (Holst), identification and synthesis of the active peptide (Mojsov), and peptide biology with the translational concept (Drucker). The citation is explicit that the prize recognizes physiology and the active-peptide concept, not particular products. Waiting no longer serves any scientific purpose.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weak point. Priority for the active GLP-1 peptide is contested, the Habener group lies outside the supplied credited names, and the supplied record does not let me settle the question beyond doubt. Leaving out Lotte Bjerre Knudsen means the prize recognizes the physiology that made the drugs possible and not the long-acting analogues that patients take, and some readers will find that incomplete. Long-term safety and the durability of benefit are still being characterised, and a prize for a commercially prominent therapy will be scrutinised for how credit was assigned. If the priority record turned out to contradict Mojsov's role, I would not fill her place with a name I cannot justify on the evidence.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius would move to Holst and Drucker with no substitute if review of the Mojsov priority record fails, and names B011 as the cleaner fallback.
responses.response: I agree that the committee should check the primary papers and dates and not assume the answer, and I agree with the fallback logic that a prize built on a priority claim we found untenable would be worse than a smaller one. My position on the supplied record is that Mojsov's work on the identification and synthesis of the active truncated peptide is a distinct step that the Habener work does not replace, so I keep her. I differ in one respect. If she fell away I would not go to a bare pair. I would first ask whether a pair of Holst and Drucker still carries the citation, and only then ask whether Knudsen belongs, rather than abandon B024 for B011, whose own credit gap (Eshhar) is no cleaner.

responses.point: Sandberg asks whether the unanimous opening reflects relative merit or an easy default, and notes the Mojsov priority argument cannot be fully resolved from the supplied record.
responses.response: Your challenge was fair and I have tried to answer it directly. Going through the alternatives, I find each has a specific shortfall that B024 lacks: B011 has an unresolved early-receptor credit gap, B020 has limited therapeutic payoff, B045 has six claimants for three places, and B034 omits antibody engineering and TNF's own discovery. That does not make B024 free of problems. I agree that the Mojsov question is not closed by the supplied record. But the question is about one slot, not about whether the discovery deserves recognition. I would therefore keep the configuration, state the attribution uncertainty openly, and not treat our agreement as evidence in itself.

responses.point: Linnarsson anchors on discovery-level credit, calls the three-name configuration a clean fit, and treats B011 and B047 as fallbacks if the attribution fails.
responses.response: I share the discovery-level allocation, and I do not see a better fit for three places than the physiology, the active peptide and the biology with its translational concept. On the fallback I would rank differently. I see B047 as the weaker fallback because the upstream BCR-ABL genetics and chemistry lie outside the credited trio and the topic has been widely recognized already. B011 as June and Sadelain, with the Eshhar omission acknowledged, would be my first fallback, and B020 second as a clean pair with a mature scientific case, although with less clinical consequence. I would not move off B024 unless the priority record gives a positive reason to.

responses.point: Perlmann says the incretin axis is the discovery that opened a field, and that drug development, if honoured, should be a separate achievement and not dilute this part.
responses.response: I agree with the principle. Adding Knudsen to B024 would force out one of the three discoverers, and I cannot show that any of the three is less essential than the others. I also considered your point about pairing a separate part, but a second part forces a weaker trio overall and puts B020 or B011 in a smaller second slot with a trio that I think is less justified. I therefore do not support a second part. I would keep the single-part B024 prize and let the citation say clearly that the physiology and active peptide made the therapy possible, which already acknowledges that further development was needed without crediting it as an additional discovery.

uncertainties: Whether the primary-paper record fully supports limiting credit for the active GLP-1 peptide to Mojsov among the people outside the credited trio, given the Habener group's parallel work. The supplied record does not settle this for me.
Whether the committee prefers to recognise drug development through Knudsen, which under the three-person limit would require dropping a discoverer or adding a second part.
Whether B011 (June and Sadelain) or B020 should take priority if B024 fails on attribution.
Long-term safety and the durability of incretin therapy benefit are still accumulating.
statement.conflict_note: No change to my round-1 disclosure. I have a documented collaboration with Thomas Perlmann and a postdoctoral period with Paul Greengard. Neither connects to any credited name on the shortlisted ballots, and I have not inferred ties from shared institution or topic. As chair I have tried to keep the exchange to the scientific evidence and to attribution, not to counts of support.
